memory_candidates.content: In this repo's manifest-routing-lib.sh, routing_lookup() only resolves two-level manifest blocks shaped {op: {task_type: value}} (routing, routing_hard, routing_agents, routing_agents_hard). A new manifest key shaped {task_type: value} (one level, no per-operation axis) needs a parallel function, not a forced reuse of routing_lookup() with a fake op key -- the shape mismatch would misrepresent the manifest schema. Mirror routing_lookup()'s same 4-step non-core/core x exact/compound precedence against a one-level jq path instead.

In this repo, /orchestrate --hard never actually invokes skill-orchestrate-hard: commands/orchestrate.md hardcodes skill: "skill-orchestrate" as its only Skill-tool target and threads effort_flag="hard" into skill-orchestrate's own delegation context, which uses it only for agent routing (command-route-agent.sh against routing_agents_hard). skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md is unreachable dead code, confirmed by a repo-wide grep for it as a Skill-tool target returning zero hits outside its own file. Any hard-mode logic addition belongs inside skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md as an if $hard_mode branch, never in the -hard file.
